notes:
Overview: mid-market ecommerce SaaS (merchant analytics + merchant-facing storefront tools). Evaluating Hosted API during 3-week trial; moving to Dedicated for predictable peak throughput and data isolation. Team: Head of Product (Ari Patel), CTO (Lina Ortiz), ML Eng (Samir Rao).

Hosted trial highlights (01/20–02/10):
- Trial run: ~3 weeks, ingest of production-like traffic via shadowing + canary routes. ~120k requests total.
- Token mix observed: ~70% short (<256 tokens), 25% medium (256–1024), 5% long (>1024). Avg tokens/request (input+output): ~480.
- Request profile: median latency (hosted) 90ms for short prompts; p95 ~320ms for medium/long.
- QPS observed: sustained 6 qps outside peak; peak sustained window ~18 qps for ~10 minutes during promotion.
- Concurrency observed: typical 8–12 concurrent connections, burst up to 30 in promo spikes.
- Cost sensitivity: product team flagged target unit economics to hit < $0.002/token effective for customer-facing inference (quoted internally).

Use-case specifics + SLAs:
- Support chatbot: latency SLO <150ms median; degraded fallback acceptable to smaller model for long-context queries.
- Checkout recommendations / reranking: needs deterministic throughput, p95 <250ms for medium-length prompts.
- Embeddings: batch offline nightly; want lower-cost quantized footprints for embeddings-heavy pipelines.

Dedicated sizing ask (why):
- Need reserved capacity to guarantee promo bursts + marketplace spikes.
- Want data isolation (PCI adjacency discussions) and audit logs; prefer VPC deployment.
- Interested in autoscale/burst policy with defined commit + burst pool.

Redwood POC feedback and technical items:
- Liked routing features: route critical endpoints to high-priority pool; non-critical to best-effort.
- Interested in automatic KV/prefix caching to reduce hot-loop token costs for support flows.
- Asked about quantized model variants for embeddings and cost trade-offs.
- Asked for guidance on batching window vs latency impact — product needs real numbers for expected p95 under batching=20ms, 50ms.

Traffic forecasting notes (internal + Redwood discussion):
- Merchant Spark provided 14 days of production traffic sample for analysis. Redwood delivered preliminary forecast:
  * Baseline QPS (business hours): 25 QPS expected in 6 months under current growth assumptions.
  * Peak QPS (promotion days): 60 QPS 10–20 minute bursts.
  * Expected concurrency requirement: 35–45 concurrent sessions at peak.
  * Token forecast (monthly): ~4.8B tokens/month (mix weighted to short+medium).
- Redwood proposed Dedicated config: 2 x 80GB GPUs (reserved) + 1 burst pool node; recommended model variants: rlhf-medium for chat, quantized-ggml for embeddings.

Commercial/contracting:
- Redwood pricing deck v2 shared (drive link above). Initial committed monthly spend under discussion: $12k–$28k/mo depending on burst policy + model choices.
- Procurement timeline: legal + security review in March; exec sign-off by end of April.

Recent activities timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-19: Intro demo (Jordan Myers) — product fit confirmed for chat + rerank. (ff_2026-01-19_merchant-spark_initial-demo)
- 2026-01-22: Hosted API onboarding + API key issued; shadow traffic enabled.

- 2026-03-05: Commercial proposal updated with dedicated sizing; pricing call scheduled.

Direct quotes / call snippets:

- "Need clear guidance on committed QPS vs observed concurrency — finance needs numbers for procurement." — Lina Ortiz, CTO.

Open technical asks for SE:
- Produce recommended Dedicated capacity table mapping expected QPS/concurrency/token mix to GPU counts and expected token cost.
- Provide benchmarks p50/p95 latency for short vs long prompts under proposed config (2x80GB + 1 burst).
- Provide batching/caching tuning guide and expected cost delta for enabling prefix caching.

Next steps (short):

- Risk: procurement may push back if dedicated ARR > $250k/year; propose staged commit with monthly true-up.
